_: The demo walk's content, shared by the no-database fallback (src/lib/demo.ts) and the seeder (scripts/seed-demo.mjs) so the two can't drift. Posts are placed by stage and a fraction along it, never by kilometre, so they survive a route:build or a fork. Days 1-3 are real photographs of the places, licensed from Wikimedia Commons: the credit at the end of those captions is the licence condition, so it travels with the picture and must not be edited out. Days 4-6 are generated placeholders in public/demo/sample, standing in where no photograph was to hand.

posts.caption: Seven in the morning at the Sé. Stamp one in the credencial and off. · photo Thomas Dahlstrøm Nielsen, CC BY 4.0
Down to the river before the city woke up. · photo Jakub Hałun, CC BY 4.0
Out of the city and onto the sea. The lighthouse at Boa Nova, and the wind arrived with it. · photo Vitor Oliveira, CC BY-SA 2.0
Twenty-eight kilometres and this at the end of them. Nine hundred arches, apparently. · photo Nmmacedo, CC BY-SA 3.0
Vila do Conde. Feet up, sardines, bed.
Pilgrim menu, twelve euros, three courses. Neither of us finished it and both of us tried.
Boardwalks the whole morning. You can hear it before you see it. · photo Francisco Restivo, CC BY 2.0
Windmills above Apúlia. They used to gather seaweed off this beach with ox carts. · photo Pedro, public domain
The Cávado at Esposende. Jit swam; Ju watched. · photo AJSL48, CC BY-SA 4.0
Esposende. Fifty-two kilometres in, and nothing has fallen off yet.
Third morning. Viana somewhere up there past the mouth of the Lima. · photo Vitor Oliveira, CC BY-SA 2.0
Over the Lima and into Viana. The bridge is Eiffel’s, apparently.
Viana do Castelo. Twenty-six more.
Wind off the Atlantic hard enough to lean on.
Lunch on a quay in a village whose name we never did catch.
That far bank is Spain. Ten days of walking and it is right there.
Caminha, and the river between us and Spain.
Boat ran. Tide was right, wind was wrong, we went anyway.
A Guarda. Spain.
The monastery at Oia, and grey water all the way to Ireland.

messages.body: Off you go then. Ring when you get there, or don’t, but eat something.
Twenty-eight kilometres on day one is showing off.
I have looked at this map four times today.
The aqueduct photo is unreal. More of those please.
Jit swimming in September. Of course.
Weather says rain Thursday. Take the good socks.
Following every step from a desk in Leeds. Buen Camino both.
That far bank is Spain. I did not think you would be there this quickly.
I have lit a candle for the boat. Tell Jit to wear the hat.
Pub quiz went badly without you. Nobody knew any geography. Buen Camino.
Six days in and you’ve made Spain. That is properly mad. More pictures please.
